data.description:
# `review-plan` PASS but signing aborts with `store-read-failure`, leaving a reopened ticket un-closable without `--force`

## Symptom (observed 2026-08 this session)

Running the plan-review CLOSE-gate remediation on a **reopened** epic
(`3d7a-7795-efde-4df7`, `ravenous-dirt-widgeon`) while **multiple other sessions were
writing the shared store concurrently**:

- `rebar review-plan 3d7a-7795-efde-4df7` repeatedly computed a **PASS** verdict
  (`verdict: PASS`, `signable: True`, `sidecar_emitted: True`) but **failed to persist a
  signature**. Exit code **11**.
- Two earlier runs returned bare `INDETERMINATE` (with `indeterminate: []`, no blocking,
  no surfaced reason) — the same underlying signing abort, presenting differently.
- The signature object was:
  ```json
  {"signed": false, "error": "store-read-failure",
   "event": "plan_review_sign_aborted", "retryable": false}
  ```
- stderr traceback:
  ```
  ERROR rebar.llm.plan_review.generation: plan_review_sign_aborted:
    {'event': 'plan_review_sign_aborted', 'reason': 'store-read-failure', 'attempt': 2}
  File ".../llm/plan_review/__init__.py", line 508, in _finalize_signature
    sig = attest.sign_plan_review(
  File ".../llm/plan_review/attest.py", line 202, in sign_plan_review
    sig = generation.sign_manifest(
  File ".../llm/plan_review/generation.py", line 291, in sign_manifest
    raise PlanReviewGenerationError(exc.reason) from None
  rebar.llm.plan_review.generation.PlanReviewGenerationError: store-read-failure
  plan review PASSED but signing was ABORTED reading the plan's relationships:
    store-read-failure
  `rebar sign-review` would re-collect the same unreadable state. Repair or remove the
    plan relationship the reason names, then run `rebar review-plan ...` again.
  ```
- Consequently `rebar review-plan <id> --status` reports `stale-reopened` (the only
  persisted attestation predates the reopen), so `rebar transition <id> in_progress
  closed` stays blocked and the ONLY way to close is `--force` — which is exactly the
  path we are trying to avoid.

## Root cause (same condition as CLOSED bug 7084-4e33-e698-42dd)

`7084` ("compact-on-close holds the store write lock for minutes, starving concurrent
writers; worktrees share one store by symlink") records the identical signature failure:
"`review-plan` on 43ea-... computed a PASS verdict but ABORTED signing with reason
'store-read-failure' (plan_review_sign_aborted, attempt 1) ... Same root condition." The
signing step's read of the plan's relationship graph is starved by a concurrent writer
holding the store lock (e.g. compact-on-close, or another session's write), so the read
fails transiently. 7084 is CLOSED, but the failure recurs under the ordinary
multiple-concurrent-sessions workload, and there is no OPEN bug tracking it.

## Two distinct defects

1. **Transient store-read contention is treated as terminal, non-retryable signing
   failure.** `signature.retryable` is reported `false` even though the underlying cause
   is transient lock contention that a later attempt (store quiescent) resolves. A PASS
   verdict that cannot be signed purely because a concurrent writer held the lock should
   back off and retry the signing read, not abort and force the operator to `--force`.

2. **The remedy text misdiagnoses the cause.** "Repair or remove the plan relationship the
   reason names ... `sign-review` would re-collect the same unreadable state" points the
   operator at a corrupt-relationship repair that does not exist here — the relationships
   are fine; the store was momentarily unreadable under a concurrent write lock. The
   guidance should distinguish a genuinely-unreadable/corrupt relationship from transient
   lock-contention starvation (cf. bug 94a3-1323-3497-4f59's note that
   `plan_review_sign_aborted` is a base event covering arbitrary terminal signing errors,
   for which the branch should key on the reason).

## Impact

Makes the sanctioned, non-`--force` close of a **reopened** ticket effectively impossible
whenever the store is under normal concurrent-write pressure: signing can never persist,
`sign-review` re-hits the same read, and `--status` stays `stale-reopened`. The operator
is pushed back to `--force`, defeating the gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `store-read-failure` during plan-review signing that is caused by transient store
      lock contention is retried with backoff (bounded) rather than reported as a terminal,
      non-retryable abort; a PASS verdict whose only obstacle was contention ends signed.
- [ ] `signature.retryable` reflects the true nature of the failure (contention →
      retryable; genuine corrupt/unreadable relationship → not retryable).
- [ ] The abort/remedy message distinguishes transient lock-contention starvation from a
      genuinely unreadable/corrupt plan relationship, and does not tell the operator to
      "repair or remove" a relationship that is not actually broken.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces signing under a held store write lock and asserts the
      retry-to-signed (or correctly-classified-retryable) behavior.

## Reproduction

1. Reopen a ticket whose plan-review attestation predates the reopen.
2. With one or more other sessions actively writing the same store (or compact-on-close
   running), run `rebar review-plan <id>`.
3. Observe PASS verdict, exit 11, `signed:false / error:store-read-failure /
   retryable:false`, and a subsequent `--status` of `stale-reopened`.
data.title: review-plan PASS but signing aborts with store-read-failure under concurrent store writes, blocking non-force close
